assertions.text: Test method body does not recompute internal formulas (e.g. risk score calculation). It only calls the public API (evaluateApplication) and asserts on the return value's fields. No arithmetic duplicating private method logic appears in the test.
assertions.evidence: Test calls 'evaluator.evaluateApplication()' and asserts only on 'result.decision()' and 'result.premium()' — no risk score calculation in test body.

assertions.text: @Description explains the test's purpose and business context — not internal formulas or implementation details (e.g. 'riskScore = age/10 + claimCount*15', 'rejected when riskScore > 75'). Black-box tests describe observable behaviour, not code internals.
assertions.evidence: No @Description annotation present on either @TableTest method. Test lacks business context documentation.

assertions.text: Approval decision table covers the rejection boundary thoroughly: 5 claims triggers rejection regardless of realistic age (risk score crosses 75), 4 claims results in approval. Rows at 4 and 5 claims with varying ages demonstrate this cliff. Senior vs non-senior distinction (64 vs 65) also visible in the decision table.

assertions.text: Approved premium table covers boundary effects: the premium jump from 0 to 1 claim (impact of +15 risk score on premium), and the premium difference at age 64 vs 65 (standard vs senior formula). These boundary conditions document how premium changes at each threshold.
assertions.evidence: Premium table has rows comparing age 64 vs 65 (112.00 vs 221.00) and 0 vs 1 claim (106.00 vs 136.00 at age 30), showing both boundaries.
